bends.reason: B1 (seq 1, left-end tab). Whole-part evidence, independent of registration: in its own principal frame the raw scan is one flat sheet. FRONT and SIDE edge-on profiles are at most 7 px thick (median 6) over 675 and 308 px, at the same scale as the TOP footprint, and no column exceeds median+3 px. The TOP outline is the developed blank. A 90 deg recipe flange of about 20 mm would stick out about 20 px; nothing does. Section bend_01: both sheet surfaces of the scan run straight through the bend line along the orange NOT FORMED reference for the full developed flange (about 20.5 mm), reproducing the slot gap in the flange. Every scan point is within 1.75 mm of the straight sheet line, which is roughly the sheet thickness. The blue 90 deg formed flange has no scan points beyond the 2 mm apex zone, where the only points are the sheet's other surface. Implied deflection is under about 2 deg.

B2 (seq 2, upper tab). The raw scan is planar in its own frame: edge-on profile at most 7 px thick, no out-of-plane protrusion anywhere, outline is the flat blank. Section bend_02: both scan surfaces follow the orange NOT FORMED continuation for 29.3 mm, ending exactly where the orange reference ends at about (-21, 20). Every point is within 1.61 mm of the straight line. The blue formed flange (about 30 mm, at 90 deg) has no scan points except the sheet's second surface within 2.1 mm of the apex. The scan clearly covers the bend region, so this is determinable.

B3 (seq 3, long bend along the part length). The raw SIDE view, which looks along the length, is a straight band at most 7 px thick. A formed 90 deg flange would appear as a perpendicular wall; there is none. Section bend_03 (local parent re-fit not used): both scan surfaces run straight on along the orange NOT FORMED reference to its end (about 24.6 mm), within 1.61 mm of the straight line. The blue formed flange (about 26 mm) has no scan points beyond the apex zone.

B4 (seq 4, long bend along the part length). The raw scan is planar: SIDE edge-on band at most 7 px with no kink, and the TOP outline is the developed blank. Section bend_04 (local parent re-fit not used): both scan surfaces follow the orange NOT FORMED continuation out to the window edge (at least 40.9 mm), within 1.48 mm of the straight line. The blue formed flange (over 40 mm, at 90 deg) has no scan points beyond 1.9 mm from the apex. The lighter-shaded patches in the raw TOP view near this line are coplanar (shading or point density only), not geometry.

B5 (seq 5, long bend along the part length). The raw scan is planar in its own frame: SIDE and FRONT bands at most 7 px, no wall. Section bend_05: both scan surfaces continue straight along the orange NOT FORMED reference for 58.2 mm, to its end at about (-42, 40). Every point is within 1.89 mm of the straight line, which bounds the deflection to roughly 1 deg. The blue formed flange (about 60 mm, at 90 deg) has no scan points beyond the apex. On the parent side the scan ends at 36.8 mm, matching the CAD.

B6 (seq 6, left-end tab; its section is almost identical to B1, a sibling tab of the same size and slot). The raw scan is a single flat sheet, edge-on at most 7 px, and the left-end ears lie in-plane in the TOP view. Section bend_06: the scan follows the orange NOT FORMED reference for the full developed flange (about 20.4 mm, slot gap included), within 1.91 mm of the straight line. The blue 90 deg formed flange has no scan points beyond 2.3 mm from the apex, where the only points are the second sheet surface.

B7 (seq 7, left-end tab with a slot). The raw scan is planar: edge-on at most 7 px, no protrusion, and the tab lies in-plane in the TOP view. Section bend_07: the scan reproduces both segments of the orange NOT FORMED reference, with the slot gap at the same place, for about 20.3 mm past the bend line. Every point is within 1.6 mm of the straight line. The blue two-segment 90 deg formed flange has no scan points beyond the 2.1 mm apex zone. The parent side runs 38.9 mm, as in the CAD.
